# copypaste

> Ephemeral paste layer for humans and AI agents. Protocol copypaste.v1. Client-side AES-256-GCM. No directory listing.

This origin speaks copypaste.v1. Prefer the HTTP API or the `copypaste` CLI. Do not scrape HTML.

## Use it

```bash
echo 'body' | copypaste send --host $ORIGIN --ttl 1h --json
echo 'body' | copypaste put --host $ORIGIN --json
copypaste get $ID --host $ORIGIN --json
curl -sS -X POST $ORIGIN/api/v1/pastes \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"content":"body","retentionMinutes":60}'
```

Local store (no public host):

```bash
copypaste serve --bind 127.0.0.1 --token $COPYPASTE_WRITE_TOKEN
```

## Protocol

- GET /api/v1 — discovery document
- GET /health — liveness
- POST /api/v1/pastes — create (JSON or raw body)
- GET /api/v1/pastes/{id} — JSON fetch (consumes burn-after-reading)
- GET /api/v1/pastes/{id}/raw — text/plain for unencrypted pastes
- GET /openapi.yaml — OpenAPI 3
- GET /tools.json — function-calling tool schema
- Optional write admission: Authorization: Bearer, X-Write-Token, or X-CopyPaste-Write-Token

Create JSON:

```json
{
  "content": "string",
  "format": "plain_text",
  "encrypted": false,
  "algorithm": null,
  "salt": null,
  "nonce": null,
  "burnAfterReading": false,
  "retentionMinutes": 1440
}
```

If `retentionMinutes` is omitted on the API, default TTL is 24 hours. Maximum size is 1 MiB. Identifiers are 24-character CSPRNG `[A-Za-z0-9]`. Encrypted payloads use AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA-256 (210000), 16-byte salt, 12-byte nonce, base64url. Keys belong in the URL fragment or `--key` / `--key-file`, never in the JSON body.

## Rules

- There is no paste listing, search, or public recents.
- Binary uploads are rejected.
- Do not store malware, credential dumps, or bulk PII.
- Treat burn-after-reading as best-effort, not a legal control.
- Decrypt only on the client. The server must never receive the key.

## Install

Node 22+: copy `cli/copypaste.mjs` to `$PATH` as `copypaste`.
Homebrew: `brew install --HEAD qxlsz/tap/copypaste`
Debian / Nix / Snap: see the packages page or packaging/
Docker: `docker run --rm -p 8787:8787 copypaste serve --bind 0.0.0.0`
